questions.q: What is a return to supplier (RTS) used for?
options: Fixing a data-entry mistake with no physical change to the goods
Reversing a receipt, in whole or in part, to send material back to the supplier due to a physical problem like damage or failed inspection
Creating a brand new purchase order
Approving a requisition on behalf of someone else
questions.explain: An RTS reflects an actual physical decision to send goods back, typically due to damage, a wrong item, or failed inspection.

questions.q: How does a correction differ from a return to supplier?
options: They are identical processes with different names
A correction can only be used for service purchase orders
A correction fixes a recording mistake made on the receiving side, without necessarily involving the supplier, while a return reflects an actual decision to send goods back
A correction always increases the received quantity, while a return always decreases it
questions.explain: A correction addresses an error in how the receipt was recorded; a return addresses a physical problem with the goods themselves and involves the supplier.

questions.q: If 5 of 50 bearings had been rejected during inspection, what would Priya most likely process?
options: A correction, since nothing physically needs to change
Nothing - rejected units are simply ignored
A full cancellation of the entire purchase order
A return to supplier for the 5 rejected units, reducing the received quantity to 45
questions.explain: Rejected units due to a physical defect would be processed as a return to supplier, reducing the quantity considered received.

questions.q: Why would an unprocessed return or correction cause a problem when Meridian's invoice arrives?
options: If the received quantity available for matching is lower than the invoiced quantity, the invoice will not match within tolerance and will be placed on hold
It would have no effect on invoice processing at all
It would automatically cancel the purchase order
It would double the amount owed to the supplier
questions.explain: A mismatch between received and invoiced quantity, caused by an unprocessed return or correction, can trigger a matching hold rather than allowing payment.

questions.q: Does LTV's main transaction in this course require a return or a correction?
options: Yes, a return is required because some bearings were rejected
Returns are required for every goods receipt as a standard step
Yes, a correction is required because Priya entered the wrong quantity
No, all 50 bearings pass inspection cleanly and the receipt is entered correctly, so neither is needed in the main scenario
questions.explain: In this course's clean main-path scenario, the shipment is received correctly and passes inspection in full, so no return or correction is needed.
